digest.component_or_area: review-bot event store and persistent clone integrity
propositions: Two untracked event JSON files exist in the persistent review-bot clone at commit HEAD = refs/remotes/origin/tickets with no merge, rebase, or stash state; they predate the A6-0b deployment and risk being overwritten or stranded by a history rewrite or reset.

The first file (TICKET_DIGEST) is a superseded unsigned derived-cache sidecar for ticket 172e-b207-4c18-4243, never committed as a canonical event; seven newer committed digests exist in the authoritative branch, making this older residue disposable.

The second file (CLAIM_ENRICH) is an expired queue claim for ticket 7ab3-9df0-7a90-4ffd with lease expiry 1785821799349015193; later authoritative claims and completion events exist, making this expired residue disposable.

Both stranded files were authorized for deletion conditional on matching recorded SHA-256 hashes, appearing in git status with no other untracked files, and HEAD remaining equal to refs/remotes/origin/tickets.

After authorized deletion via SSM command f91a67cd-9b62-485c-92f9-64d116837159, the persistent clone achieved clean state: HEAD = origin/tickets, empty git status, no merge/rebase/stash artifacts, and no unique canonical events lost.

Acceptance criteria evidence labels were corrected from [code-verifiable] to [operator-attested] to align with the concrete ticket operator attestations and clean-clone receipt recorded in the SSM response, without weakening scope or success threshold.
